findings.title: Payment is recast as protective separation
findings.claim: The offered payment and the requested barrier are joined as two applications of a state-changing act: resources are converted into a protective separation that interrupts corruption.
findings.mechanism: The two focus occurrences of جَعَلَ carry the accepted state-change branch, while خَرْجًا, the duplicated بَيْنَ relation, and سَدًّا supply distinct objects and relations; the supplied 18:52 and 47:22 connections make the barrier's function legible as interruption of harmful contact and social rupture.
findings.reader_payoff: The request becomes a proposal to change the relation through which harm reaches the people, so the barrier's value lies in the contact it interrupts as well as in its material presence.
findings.containment: The plain request for a paid barrier remains intact. This adds a qualified relational reading and does not identify every intervening structure with the supplied parallels.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run publication supplies exact focus anchors and a trusted branch claim; the reader-walk support and the wider connection preserve the relational elaboration, while the connection target's missing morphology keeps the extended resonance qualified.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: birini veya şeyi belirli bir duruma getirme
branch_activations.facet_statement: Var olan bir katılımcının durumunu, niteliğini veya konumunu değiştiren ettirici işlemi bildirir.
branch_activations.carrier: جَعَلَ in نَجْعَلُ and تَجْعَلَ carries the act of bringing an existing participant into a changed state or position.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The separate objects and relation are payment (خَرْجًا), the duplicated between phrase, and سَدًّا, with the 18:52 barrier parallel and the 47:22 corruption-and-social-rupture parallel supplying wider activation.
branch_activations.activation: Because the same state-changing carrier governs both the proposed compensation and the requested barrier, the wider parallels make the requested change legible as protection that alters harmful contact, not merely as paid construction.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The proposal asks for a changed relation between the community and corruption, with the barrier's value measured by the harmful contact it interrupts.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not claim that every between-structure has the same moral value or that 18:52 is the same event; it uses only the supplied parallel and focus relation.

findings.title: Community value becomes shared protective contribution
findings.claim: The offered خَرْجًا can be heard as value moving out of the community while remaining a financial obligation, and the wider construction is supplied by shared strength and material contribution.
findings.mechanism: The focus noun carries both the outward-movement branch and the financial-value branch; the supplied reader-walk support names the later request for strength and the delivery of iron and labor, while the 18:77 and 23:72 connections sharpen the payment-and-protection relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The people's offer opens from a fee into a picture of protection built by resources leaving the community in the form the work requires.
findings.containment: The word's financial sense remains present. The later participatory application does not redefine every payment or claim that خَرْجًا itself names iron or labor.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run publication gives a trusted focus-anchored contribution claim; the wide reader-walk supplies the 18:95-96 application, and the connection targets provide exact Arabic but no target morphology, so the contextual extension remains qualified.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied later-pericope account asks for strength and receives iron and labor, while the 18:77 and 23:72 connections place payment beside protective construction and its refusal.

findings.title: The barrier has a bounded protective horizon
findings.claim: The requested سَدًّا can carry a protective function whose effectiveness belongs to a bounded period and whose wider horizon includes the later opening of the restrained peoples.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier names an obstacle placed between sides; the supplied 18:82 connection parallels a wall that preserves vulnerable heirs as mercy, while 21:96 and the immediate 18:99 continuation supply the later opening and surge that bound the protection in time.
findings.reader_payoff: The set becomes a material act of care whose protection matters for a period and whose later opening belongs to the same image without erasing the care it provided.
findings.containment: This does not import a construction recipe, assert literal demolition inside 18:94, or claim that the target ayahs share morphology; it uses their supplied structural relations and exact target Arabic only.

epistemic.reason: The connection rows provide exact target Arabic and explicit relation notes but no target morphology or trust label; the protective-horizon activation is therefore retained as a qualified structural resonance.

branch_activations.carrier: سَدًّا carries the obstacle-between-sides sense: an opening is closed by an intervening barrier that covers what lies behind it.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The supplied wider relations pair protective mercy for vulnerable heirs at 18:82 with the later release of Ya'juj and Ma'juj at 21:96 and the surge described at 18:99.
branch_activations.activation: The barrier's focus function contacts both preservation and later opening, so closure is legible as protective care with a temporal horizon rather than as an unbounded final condition.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The set is a protective intervention whose effectiveness belongs to a period of restraint, while its wider horizon includes the opening that follows.
branch_activations.boundary: The finding does not claim that 18:94 itself narrates the later opening, nor that the connection targets provide a shared lexical branch or construction detail.
